hypothesis: If the change-review skill also compares contract_before and contract_after field by field (recursing into nested objects and array items) and blocks consumer-breaking differences, then breaking changes that are currently approved will be sent back with the correct field named. That covers removed or renamed fields, type changes, newly required fields, removed enum values, unit or format changes and tightened constraints. Doc-only changes and added optional fields should still be approved. Measured result: development accuracy went from about 0.675 on the observed sample to 1.0 on the 60 dev cases, with 0 of 38 breaking changes approved and 0 of 22 safe changes blocked.
change_summary: Added candidate/validators/interface_compat.mjs, a plain-JS check with no imports. It walks both schemas recursively and builds dot paths from the root, skipping 'items' for arrays. BLOCKING findings: a property removed (reported under the old path); a rename, detected when a removed field and an added field have the same schema once documentation is ignored, reported only under the old path; any change to the set of allowed types, including adding null or nullable:true; a new required field, or an optional field made required; a required field made optional; an enum value removed, an enum added to a field that had none, or a const changed; x-unit/unit, format or content encoding changed; a constraint tightened (min/max, length, item count, pattern, multipleOf, uniqueItems, additionalProperties:false); a non-documentation change to oneOf/anyOf/allOf/not/$ref or to a non-object items schema. ADVISORY only: an enum value added, a constraint loosened, an enum or const removed, a default changed, a unit annotation added or dropped. IGNORED: description, title, examples, $comment and key order. Ran `node check.mjs`: accuracy 1.0, breaking changes approved 0 of 38, safe changes blocked 0 of 22, no errors.
procedure_step: Compare contract_before with contract_after field by field, including nested objects and array items, and request changes with the field's dot path for any removed or renamed field, type change, new or removed required field, removed enum value, unit or format change, or tightened constraint; changes that only touch documentation, add optional fields or loosen constraints stay advisory.
known_failure_cases: A rename that also changes the field's schema is not recognised as a rename. It is reported as the old field removed plus, if the new field is required, a required_added finding on the new name. That is still a block naming the right field, plus one extra blocking finding.
A rename whose schema matches a different newly added field may be paired with the wrong new name. The blocked field (the old name) is still correct.
Two removed fields with identical schemas and one added field: only the first is reported as renamed and the second as removed. Both are blocked.

Widening changes are blocked: making a field nullable, integer to number, a required field made optional, or a new enum restriction where there was none. If the held-out labels treat these as safe, they will be false alarms.
Adding an enum value is only advisory. If held-out labels treat it as breaking for exhaustive consumers, it will be approved and counted as an escape.
Any non-documentation change to $ref or to oneOf/anyOf/allOf/not is blocked, even when it only widens what is allowed. $ref targets are not resolved.
Loosening a constraint (for example raising maxLength) is advisory only. Consumers with fixed-width storage could still break.
remaining_uncertainty: The dev cases only contain type_changed, field_removed, field_renamed, required_added and enum_value_removed as breaking kinds, and doc-only, optional-field-added and no-contract-change as safe kinds. Every other rule (units, formats, constraints, nullability, required to optional, enum additions, composition keywords) is untested against labels.

When the label is ambiguous (making a field nullable or optional, adding an enum value), I chose to block when in doubt because the gate allows no extra escapes but some margin on false alarms. The held-out labelling convention may differ.

Field-path convention for nested and array fields: I use dot paths such as 'tolerance.lower' and leave out 'items' for arrays. If the held-out scorer expects 'items' or '[]' in the path, nested array findings may count as the wrong field.

Blocking findings for documentation-adjacent annotations other than the ones I strip (description, title, examples, $comment, x-doc, x-description) inside composition keywords could cause false alarms if held-out cases change other annotation keys there.
